scenes.visual: close-up illustration of the front corner of a car on a foggy night road, the small round fog light set low in the bumper glowing bright warm orange as the brightest thing in the frame, a soft flat orange beam spreading low across the road, the main headlight above it dim, pale fog filling the space above, the bumper and fog light big in the lower two-thirds of the frame, simple dark blue background, no text, no logos, no number plate
scenes.narration: Why are fog lights so *low*, down by the bumper?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a car in fog, side view; a beam from headlight height goes up into the fog, droplets bounce rays back at the driver's eye one by one, the counter climbs to 18 and the windscreen glows white: WHITE WALL
scenes.narration: Fog is tiny water *droplets*. They bounce your headlights straight back into your eyes. So, the trick? Height.
scenes.headline: STEP 1/3: *DROPLETS*

scenes.visual: illustration of a person in a hooded jacket on a misty night path holding a small modern battery-powered handheld flashlight (an electric torch with a plastic body and a round lens, NO flame, NO fire) up beside their face and pointing it forward, the flashlight beam lighting the mist right in front of their face into a bright warm orange-white glowing haze that is the brightest thing in the frame, the person squinting, the face and flashlight in the middle of the frame between 35 and 65 percent of the height, plain cool dark blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Like a torch, a flashlight, on a misty night. Up by your face, the mist glows *white*. Down at your feet? You see the path.
scenes.headline: LIKE A *TORCH*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the light drops from headlight height to knee height by the bumper, the beam flattens with a sharp top edge onto the road, the bounce-back counter falls from 18 to 3, the road lines light up: ROAD LIT
scenes.narration: So fog lights sit around *knee* height, with a wide, flat beam aimed down. And there's one more trick.
scenes.headline: STEP 2/3: AIM *LOW*

scenes.visual: side-view cutaway illustration of a car on a road at night, a thick layer of pale grey fog floating above the road with a thin clearer gap of air just above the road surface, a flat bright warm orange beam from a low light on the bumper sliding through that gap and lighting the road ahead as the brightest thing in the frame, the car and road big in the lower two-thirds of the frame, simple dark blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Fog often hangs just *above* the road, so the low beam slips under it.
scenes.headline: STEP 3/3: *UNDER* IT

scenes.visual: driver's-eye view illustration from inside a car looking through the windscreen at a foggy night road, two relaxed hands on the steering wheel at the bottom, the road surface and white lane lines just ahead lit by a flat warm orange glow as the brightest thing in the frame, the fog above the road dim and soft, simple uncluttered composition, no text or logos
scenes.narration: So they're low on purpose. <short pause> They light the *road*, not the fog. Send this to whoever uses high beams in fog.
scenes.headline: THE *ROAD*, NOT THE FOG

youtube.description:
Why are fog lights low on a car? Fog is tiny water droplets, and they bounce headlight beams straight back into the driver's eyes: a white wall. So how do fog lights work? They sit low on the bumper, around knee height, and throw a wide, flat beam with a sharp top edge, aimed down at the road. Fog often hangs a little above the road, so that low beam slips under it and lights the road instead of the fog. That's fog lights vs headlights.
